title: What not to automate: the test that costs more than the defect

videos.script: This is the last lesson, and it is about the tests you should not write. {{suite}} By now your project has a few dozen tests. Each one took time to write. Each one costs a little more every time the shop changes, every time it runs, and every time it goes red for nothing. {{model}} So a test is an investment, and some investments lose money. This lesson puts numbers on two tests from this course. {{experiment}} The sideways check from lesson 7 costs almost nothing, and it found a real defect. A screenshot of the whole page fails on every change to the look. That includes the changes somebody meant. {{list}} Then the cases a robot should leave alone. A first look at a new feature. A judgement about colour or wording. A page that belongs to another company. A CAPTCHA, which exists to stop robots. {{known}} Then the tests that document a known defect, and what happens to each one the day the shop is fixed. {{run}} You run the whole suite one last time, and read it as a product, with a budget. {{map}} And the course ends with a map of what you built, lesson by lesson, and where it goes next.
